After you change your password you stay signed in here, and your other devices are signed out.

A forecast estimates how many units of a product will sell on each of the next days. The simple forecast expects every day to sell what the product sold on its most recent recorded day. The AI forecast learns from your shop\'s sales history.

AI forecasts unlock once your shop has enough sales history. Open AI model (Home, or the ⋮ menu) to see how far along you are. The AI is only used if it beats the simple forecast on your own recent sales.
Lower error means it did better on that sample, not that it will do better tomorrow. About 4% of 7-day forecasts run high, so treat a week-ahead figure as a guide rather than a promise.

1. Set up your shop.
2. Upload your sales history (Sales tab).
3. Forecast every product (Forecasts tab, or Forecast all on Home).
4. After a few months of sales, train your AI model (AI model, on Home).

A CSV file with one row per product per day: the date, the product\'s name or code, and the units sold. Price and category are optional. From Excel or Google Sheets, use Save as or Download and choose CSV. Upload more sales any time; the app adds them to what it has.
Your columns can have other names; you match them on the next screens. Using a spreadsheet? Save it as CSV first.

Use the sample file: 300 days of sales for a small mini-market with 26 products, up to yesterday. It\'s enough to try everything, including AI forecasts. Its sales are added to this shop, so use a shop you set up for practice.
Save a copy of the sample file

This shop has no sales yet. Ask the owner or a manager to upload them.

A model trained on your own shop\'s sales. It learns patterns such as busier weekends, paydays and holidays. The app only uses it if it beat the simple forecast when tested on your recent sales; otherwise you get the simple forecast.

Each coming day is expected to sell what the product sold on its most recent day with recorded sales. For example, if milk sold 12 that day, the 7-day simple forecast is 12 a day, 84 in total.\n\nIt needs no training, so it works from your first upload, and it\'s the forecast the AI has to beat. It doesn\'t know about busy weekends, paydays or holidays, and one unusual day is repeated for the whole period. Those are what the AI learns.

The app hides your last 4 weeks of sales, forecasts them, and compares the forecast with what really sold. Once real sales come in for a forecast's days, it is checked against those too.

Average miss (MAE): units off on a typical day.
Typical miss (RMSE): like the average miss, but big misses count more.
Miss as a share of sales (WAPE): all units missed divided by all units sold.

Lower is better. Doing well on past weeks is a good sign, not a promise about tomorrow.
A product is ready when it has enough recent days of sales recorded, without too many gaps. Products that aren\'t ready still get the simple forecast.

Training builds an AI model from your shop\'s sales history and takes a few minutes. The new model is tested on your last 4 weeks of sales and only used if it beats the simple forecast. After that, it is retrained each week when new sales have been added.
